title: Lucid Reveals New Cosmos Images, Says Sportier Gravity Coming Soon
summary: The Cosmos has a sloping roofline and could start production next year, while the hi-po Gravity is coming much sooner.
whatHappening: Lucid Motors has unveiled new images of its upcoming Cosmos model, revealing a sleek design with a sloping roofline. The company is also promising a high-performance variant of its Gravity SUV sooner than initially expected.
whoInvolved: Lucid Motors is an American EV manufacturer headquartered in Newark, California, which began producing the Lucid Air sedan in 2021 and started Gravity SUV production in December 2024. The company is now expanding its lineup with new models and performance variants.
whyMatters: The Cosmos and sportier Gravity represent Lucid's strategy to broaden its product range beyond the Air sedan and capture different market segments in the growing luxury EV space. Accelerating the high-performance Gravity's arrival could help Lucid compete more effectively against established luxury automakers while ramping up overall production volumes.
articleBody:
Lucid Motors is moving forward with its expansion plans, revealing new imagery of the upcoming Cosmos model while signaling that a more powerful version of its Gravity SUV will arrive ahead of schedule. According to Car and Driver, the Cosmos features a distinctive sloping roofline and could begin production as soon as next year, positioning it as another key addition to Lucid's growing electric vehicle lineup.

The Cosmos represents Lucid's third vehicle offering, following the Lucid Air sedan, which the company began manufacturing at its Casa Grande, Arizona factory in September 2021, and the Lucid Gravity SUV, which launched production in December 2024. The mid-size luxury crossover Gravity has already established itself as the brand's first SUV and second vehicle overall, arriving with a multitude of features and amenities aimed at the premium market segment.

The high-performance variant of the Gravity is particularly notable given its accelerated timeline. By bringing the sportier iteration to market sooner than previously announced, Lucid aims to offer customers a more dynamic option within its SUV portfolio while capitalizing on growing consumer interest in performance-oriented electric vehicles. This move suggests the company is confident in its production capabilities and supply chain as it scales manufacturing operations.

Lucid's portfolio expansion comes as the company continues to establish itself as both a direct automaker and a technology supplier. Beyond manufacturing its own vehicles, Lucid supplies advanced electric vehicle powertrain systems to other automakers, including Aston Martin, diversifying its revenue streams and leveraging its engineering expertise across the industry.

The introduction of the Cosmos adds another dimension to Lucid's strategy, targeting customers who may seek a different design language or market positioning than the Air or Gravity. With potential production starting next year, the timeline suggests the company has finalized development and is preparing manufacturing infrastructure to support the new model.

As Lucid navigates an increasingly competitive luxury EV market, the combination of new model launches and accelerated high-performance variants underscores the company's commitment to offering diverse options within its growing product family.

title: 2027 Kia Telluride X-Pro Test: Future-Proofed
summary: How compromised is the off-roadiest Telluride?
whatHappening: Car and Driver has tested the 2027 Kia Telluride X-Pro, the automaker's most off-road-capable variant of its three-row crossover SUV. The review examines how much capability Kia has engineered into the model and where it may have compromised practicality or on-road performance.
whoInvolved: Kia Corporation, South Korea's second-largest automobile manufacturer, is behind the Telluride line. The vehicle itself is a mid-size crossover SUV with three-row seating that Kia has produced since 2019, competing in one of the market's most popular segments.
whyMatters: The X-Pro variant signals Kia's push to capture buyers interested in both family hauling and light off-road capability—a growing market segment. The test results will influence perceptions of whether Kia's premium crossover can deliver genuine terrain prowess without sacrificing the comfort and utility that drive mainstream crossover sales.
articleBody:
Kia is making another bid for adventure-minded families with the 2027 Telluride X-Pro, its most rugged interpretation yet of the popular mid-size crossover. The X-Pro trim represents the automaker's effort to inject genuine off-road credibility into a platform best known for three-row seating and family-friendly features. According to Car and Driver, the central question driving the test was how far Kia could push the Telluride's off-road credentials without compromising the on-road refinement and practicality that have made the model a staple since its 2019 debut.

The Telluride itself has evolved into a cornerstone of Kia's global lineup. Since launching over five years ago, the crossover has captured significant market share in the three-row segment, appealing to buyers seeking a balance of space, comfort, and value. The X-Pro variant builds on that foundation by introducing enhancements aimed at rough terrain: upgraded suspension geometry, skid protection, all-terrain tires, and increased ground clearance. The model's positioning suggests Kia sees an opportunity to compete with slightly more rugged competitors while keeping the vehicle accessible to mainstream buyers.

Kia Corporation, headquartered in Seoul, has been aggressive in diversifying its model range and pushing upmarket in recent years. As South Korea's second-largest automaker after its parent company Hyundai Motor Company, Kia has the engineering resources and global distribution to test markets that rivals might avoid. The X-Pro variant of the Telluride represents a calculated bet that customers in key markets will embrace a crossover that can handle both school runs and weekend off-road excursions.

The test itself probes a fundamental tension in modern vehicle design: how much off-road performance can engineers layer onto a platform optimized for everyday comfort without introducing penalties in fuel economy, cargo space, or ride quality. Adding skid plates, all-terrain rubber, and suspension reinforcement increases weight and complexity. The challenge for Kia was ensuring those additions enhance capability without turning the Telluride into a vehicle that feels over-engineered for the mild off-roading most owners will actually attempt.

Results from this kind of hands-on assessment matter because they shape buyer confidence in a brand's claims. If the X-Pro delivers genuine terrain-handling improvements without sacrificing the refinement that made the standard Telluride appealing, it could broaden the crossover's appeal. Conversely, if compromises prove too severe, the variant risks alienating both mainstream buyers and serious off-road enthusiasts. The outcome will likely influence Kia's next steps in its adventure-focused product strategy.

title: The 2027 Polaris RZR Pro R Boost Is the Most Powerful Side-by-Side
summary: In the world of side-by-sides, no amount of horsepower is ever enough.
whatHappening: Polaris has unveiled the 2027 RZR Pro R Boost, a new side-by-side vehicle that sets a new power benchmark for the recreational off-road market. The latest iteration pushes horsepower to previously unseen levels in its class.
whoInvolved: Polaris Inc., an American automotive manufacturer headquartered in Medina, Minnesota, is releasing this vehicle. The company, which has engineered and manufactured vehicles in Roseau, Minnesota since its founding there, has a long history of producing recreational powersports vehicles beyond its well-known motorcycle brands.
whyMatters: The 2027 RZR Pro R Boost signals that manufacturers continue to escalate performance specs in the competitive side-by-side segment, where power output has become a key differentiator. For enthusiasts and buyers in this market, the vehicle represents the current pinnacle of what the category can deliver in terms of raw capability.
articleBody:
Polaris has announced the 2027 RZR Pro R Boost, the latest addition to its side-by-side vehicle lineup and a machine engineered to claim the title of most powerful in its class. According to Car and Driver, the powersports industry shows no signs of moderating horsepower ambitions, with manufacturers locked in an ongoing competition to deliver maximum performance.

The RZR Pro R Boost builds on Polaris's long track record in the recreational off-road vehicle market. Polaris Inc., headquartered in Medina, Minnesota, has maintained engineering and manufacturing operations in Roseau, Minnesota since the company's founding there, allowing the firm to develop and refine vehicles tailored to off-road enthusiasts. The RZR Pro R line has been a flagship offering within the broader side-by-side category, and this newest generation pushes the envelope further.

Side-by-side vehicles, also known as utility terrain vehicles or UTVs, have evolved dramatically over the past two decades from bare-bones utility machines into high-performance recreational platforms. The 2027 model year intensifies this trend by focusing on what many buyers in this segment prioritize: maximum engine output and acceleration capability.

The decision to boost the Pro R's power reflects market demand from a customer base that views horsepower as a core value proposition. Owners in this category often use their vehicles for both recreational trail riding and competitive events, where performance advantages translate directly into capability and bragging rights.

Polaris faces competition from other major powersports manufacturers in the side-by-side space, yet the company continues to invest in pushing performance boundaries. The 2027 RZR Pro R Boost represents a continuation of this strategy, targeting buyers who view their vehicles as premium, high-powered machines rather than basic utility tools.

title: Limited Edition Lamborghini Revuelto Celebrates the Iconic Miura
summary: Lamborghini is building 99 special-edition Revueltos with Miura-inspired colors, liveries, and interior details to honor the legendary Miura's 60th anniversary.
whatHappening: Lamborghini is producing 99 limited-edition Revueltos inspired by the legendary Miura, featuring special colors, liveries, and interior details that pay homage to the iconic 1960s sports car. The special run marks the Miura's 60th anniversary.
whoInvolved: Lamborghini, the Italian automaker, is behind the initiative. The Miura, produced between 1966 and 1973, was a groundbreaking mid-engine sports car that set the standard for high-performance road cars. The Revuelto, unveiled in 2023, is its modern successor as Lamborghini's flagship hybrid sports car.
whyMatters: This limited edition bridges Lamborghini's storied past with its electrified future, reinforcing brand heritage at a pivotal moment as the industry shifts toward hybrid and electric powertrains. For collectors and enthusiasts, it represents a rare intersection of nostalgia and cutting-edge technology, likely commanding premium values and sustained collector interest.
articleBody:
Lamborghini is honoring one of automotive history's most influential designs by producing just 99 special-edition Revueltos inspired by the iconic Miura. According to Car and Driver, the limited run features Miura-inspired colors, liveries, and interior details that celebrate the legendary sports car's 60th anniversary.

The Miura holds a unique place in automotive lore. Produced between 1966 and 1973, it was the first high-performance production road car to feature a rear mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout—a configuration that has since become the standard for performance-oriented sports cars worldwide. When it debuted, the Miura was the fastest production car in the world, cementing Lamborghini's reputation as a builder of extraordinary machines.

The Revuelto, which succeeded the Aventador following its official unveiling on March 29, 2023, represents Lamborghini's evolution into the hybrid era. Named after a Spanish fighting bull that fought in Barcelona's arena during the 1880s, the Revuelto is a mid-engine plug-in hybrid that marries contemporary engineering with the brand's performance DNA. By applying Miura design cues to this modern platform, Lamborghini creates a visual and thematic connection across six decades of innovation.

Limited-edition heritage models serve multiple purposes for luxury manufacturers. They celebrate pivotal moments in brand history while creating exclusivity that appeals to collectors and enthusiasts willing to pay premiums for distinctive variants. The 99-unit production cap ensures scarcity, a critical factor in the collector market.

The special edition underscores Lamborghini's confidence in the Revuelto as a worthy successor to its lineage. Rather than abandoning the performance identity established by the Miura, the company is explicitly linking past and future. This approach signals to the market that electrification need not mean abandonment of the brand's core values of speed, design innovation, and engineering audacity.

title: 2027 Genesis GV60 / GV60 Magma
summary: Review, Pricing, and Specs
whatHappening: Car and Driver has published a comprehensive review, pricing breakdown, and specifications for the 2027 Genesis GV60 and its high-performance Magma variant. The coverage arrives as Genesis prepares to introduce these electric vehicles to the market.
whoInvolved: Genesis is the luxury electric vehicle brand under the Hyundai Motor Group, a South Korean chaebol headquartered in Seoul that has emerged as a major player in the global automotive industry. Car and Driver is a leading automotive journalism publication providing detailed vehicle analysis and market information.
whyMatters: The GV60 and GV60 Magma represent Genesis's continued push into the premium electric vehicle segment, a category where luxury automakers are competing intensely. Detailed pricing and specifications help consumers and industry observers understand how Genesis positions these vehicles against competitors in an increasingly crowded EV market.
articleBody:
Car and Driver has released a comprehensive guide to the upcoming 2027 Genesis GV60 and GV60 Magma, offering readers detailed information about pricing, performance specifications, and design features. The coverage provides potential buyers and automotive enthusiasts with the technical data and market positioning needed to evaluate these electric luxury vehicles as they prepare for market entry.

The GV60 line represents Genesis's commitment to the electric vehicle category, where the brand aims to establish itself as a premium alternative in the rapidly expanding luxury EV segment. According to Car and Driver, the publication's review and specification breakdown covers the distinctions between the standard GV60 and the more performance-oriented Magma variant, allowing consumers to understand the differences in capability and pricing between the two models.

Genesis operates as the luxury division of the Hyundai Motor Group, a South Korean chaebol headquartered in Seoul that manages multiple automotive brands and has invested heavily in electrification across its portfolio. This corporate backing provides Genesis with significant resources for research, development, and manufacturing of advanced electric vehicles. The 2027 GV60 and Magma are products of this broader strategic commitment to offer luxury consumers compelling alternatives to established competitors in the EV space.

The detailed specifications and pricing information covered in the Car and Driver review help contextualize these vehicles within the current market. As more luxury automakers introduce electric models, understanding the specific features, performance metrics, and cost of entry for vehicles like the GV60 becomes increasingly important for consumers evaluating their options. The Magma variant, in particular, signals Genesis's intention to compete not just on luxury and efficiency but also on driving performance and driving engagement.

These vehicles arrive at a critical moment in the automotive industry's transition toward electrification. The 2027 model year positions Genesis to capture consumers seeking premium electric vehicles with advanced technology and refined design. The availability of pricing and detailed specifications through publications like Car and Driver ensures that information about these vehicles reaches potential buyers and influences broader market perception of Genesis's capabilities in the luxury EV segment.

title: View Interior Photos of the 2026 Porsche 911 GT3
summary: See the interior of the 2026 Porsche 911 GT3 from every angle.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is publishing interior photography of the upcoming 2026 Porsche 911 GT3, offering enthusiasts a detailed look at the cabin design from multiple angles. The images showcase the high-performance variant's interior before the model reaches dealerships.
whoInvolved: Porsche, the German luxury sports car manufacturer headquartered in Stuttgart, is revealing the 2026 911 GT3, the latest iteration of its iconic rear-engine performance line that has been continuously refined since its 1964 debut. Car and Driver, a major automotive publication, is providing the exclusive interior photo gallery.
whyMatters: Interior design reveals signal the direction of Porsche's technology and ergonomic philosophy for its most track-focused 911 variant, giving potential buyers and enthusiasts insight into the cabin experience before official launch. The 911 GT3 represents a pinnacle of the 911 lineage, and detailed looks at its interior help establish expectations for performance-car luxury and functionality in the coming model year.
articleBody:
Porsche is preparing to launch the 2026 911 GT3, and Car and Driver reports that the sports car's interior design is now visible through comprehensive photography. The images reveal the cabin from every angle, providing an intimate look at how Porsche has equipped this latest generation of its most celebrated performance model.

The 911 GT3 sits atop Porsche's 911 lineup as a driver-focused, track-capable variant. The Porsche 911 model series, introduced in September 1964, has maintained its core identity as a two-door, high-performance rear-engine sports car across eight generations. The 911 is defined by its rear-mounted flat-six engine and 2+2 seating configuration, though special variants have offered pure two-seater layouts. What began as an air-cooled, torsion-bar-suspended design has evolved significantly, with the 911 undergoing continuous improvements and modernization while preserving the essential engineering philosophy that made it legendary.

The GT3 variant represents the pinnacle of driver engagement within the 911 family. These images showcase Porsche's approach to the cabin in the 2026 model year, revealing how the manufacturer balances performance-oriented features with the luxury and refinement expected from the brand. The photography captures details that range from steering wheel design to instrument cluster layout to seat construction, offering enthusiasts a comprehensive view of the driving environment.

Porsche, owned by Volkswagen AG and headquartered in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, has built its reputation on producing high-performance sports cars that blend engineering excellence with practical daily usability. The 911 remains the company's flagship model, anchoring a current lineup that also includes the Panamera, Macan, Cayenne, and Taycan. For the 2026 model year, the GT3 continues that tradition of performance and refinement.

These interior photographs arrive as Porsche builds anticipation for the 2026 911 GT3's arrival. For potential buyers and automotive enthusiasts, the detailed views provide a clearer sense of how the cabin has been refined for the latest generation—what materials have been chosen, how controls are organized, and what visual language Porsche has adopted to reinforce the car's performance credentials.

title: View Photos of the 2001 Roush Stage 3 Mustang
summary: See the interior and exterior of the 2001 Roush Stage 3 Mustang from every angle.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is showcasing a visual gallery of the 2001 Roush Stage 3 Mustang, offering detailed photography of both the car's interior and exterior from multiple angles. The feature provides an in-depth look at this high-performance variant of Ford's iconic muscle car.
whoInvolved: Roush Performance, the American automotive company founded by Jack Roush in 1995, engineered and developed the Stage 3 package for the 2001 Ford Mustang. The Ford Mustang itself has been in continuous production since 1964 and serves as the namesake of the entire "pony car" segment.
whyMatters: This visual documentation preserves the design and engineering details of a significant performance variant from the early 2000s, offering enthusiasts and historians a comprehensive record of Roush's modifications to one of America's most recognizable automobiles. For collectors and fans of both the Mustang and Roush Performance, such galleries serve as valuable references for understanding the evolution of street performance engineering during that era.
articleBody:
Car and Driver presents an extensive photographic tour of the 2001 Roush Stage 3 Mustang, capturing the performance-enhanced muscle car from every conceivable angle. The gallery showcases both the vehicle's aggressive exterior styling and its carefully appointed interior, offering enthusiasts a detailed visual record of this significant performance variant.

Roush Performance, founded in 1995 by automotive mogul Jack Roush, has built its reputation on engineering and manufacturing high-performance components for both street and competitive racing applications. The Stage 3 package represented the company's commitment to extracting maximum performance from the Ford Mustang platform, a car that has maintained continuous production since 1964 and effectively created the "pony car" segment that defines American automotive culture.

The 2001 model year placed the Roush Stage 3 variant during a transitional period for the Mustang, bridging the fourth generation that had debuted in 1994 and the eventual introduction of the fifth generation in 2005. During this era, Roush's aftermarket enhancements allowed performance-focused buyers to elevate their Mustangs beyond factory specifications, whether for street driving or track use.

According to Car and Driver, the photographic documentation includes comprehensive views of the vehicle's exterior modifications, interior trim, and performance details. Such galleries serve an important archival function, preserving the specific design language and engineering choices of a particular moment in automotive performance history. For collectors, prospective buyers, and automotive historians, these visual records provide invaluable reference materials.

The emphasis on multi-angle photography reflects the growing importance of visual documentation in automotive media. By presenting the 2001 Roush Stage 3 Mustang from every perspective, the feature allows viewers to appreciate both the aesthetics of Roush's modifications and the practical engineering that distinguishes high-performance variants from standard production models.

title: This Chinese Electric Sports Car Has Nearly 430 HP and Costs About $34K
summary: Not only does it cost about the same as a four-cylinder Ford Mustang, but it's also claimed to weigh around 3000 pounds.
whatHappening: A Chinese electric sports car is entering the market with impressive performance specs and an accessible price point. The vehicle delivers nearly 430 horsepower, weighs around 3,000 pounds, and costs approximately $34,000—positioning it as a direct competitor to traditional gas-powered sports cars.
whoInvolved: A Chinese automaker is behind this electric sports car, challenging established American manufacturers like Ford. The comparison to the Ford Mustang, America's iconic pony car in continuous production since 1964, highlights the competitive shift in the automotive market.
whyMatters: This vehicle demonstrates that electric performance cars are becoming affordable and competitive with traditional sports cars at mainstream price points. The announcement signals an acceleration in global EV adoption and suggests Chinese manufacturers are capturing significant market share in the performance segment.
articleBody:
A new Chinese electric sports car is shaking up the automotive market with performance credentials that rival established American competitors at a fraction of the expected cost. According to Car and Driver, the vehicle offers nearly 430 horsepower and weighs approximately 3,000 pounds—figures that put it in direct competition with traditional gas-powered sports cars like the Ford Mustang.

The Ford Mustang, which has held the title of America's longest continuously produced nameplate since 1964, essentially created the "pony car" segment with its distinctive long hood and short deck proportions. The Mustang's success established a formula for affordable, stylish performance that has defined American automotive culture for decades. The new Chinese EV's pricing at roughly $34,000—comparable to a four-cylinder Ford Mustang—suggests that electric vehicles are now capable of delivering similar value propositions to consumers seeking sporty performance without premium pricing.

The specifications are noteworthy not just for their performance metrics but for what they represent about manufacturing efficiency. A nearly 430-horsepower vehicle weighing around 3,000 pounds indicates advanced engineering in battery integration and lightweight design. This combination of power and weight represents the kind of performance envelope that traditionally required expensive exotic engineering, now apparently achievable at mainstream prices.

The introduction of this vehicle underscores the rapid advancement of electric vehicle technology beyond niche or luxury segments. Where EVs were once viewed primarily as practical commuter vehicles or premium offerings, this sports car demonstrates that electrification can deliver genuine driving excitement at accessible price points. The weight figure is particularly significant—lighter vehicles typically deliver better acceleration and handling regardless of powertrain type, and achieving that with an electric drivetrain suggests sophisticated design choices.

For consumers, this development means that the performance car market is expanding beyond traditional boundaries. Buyers can now consider electric alternatives with genuine performance credibility at price points previously reserved for conventional sports cars. The longer-term implication is that traditional automakers may face increased pressure to compete on price and performance in the electric segment, particularly as Chinese manufacturers demonstrate capability in combining affordability with engineering sophistication.

title: This Could Be the Most Expensive McLaren F1 of All Time
summary: One of the incredibly rare F1 GTRs is headed to auction in Monterey next month, and bids could exceed $35 million.
whatHappening: A rare McLaren F1 GTR is heading to auction at Monterey Car Week next month, with expected bids potentially reaching $35 million or more. This could set a new record as the most expensive McLaren F1 ever sold.
whoInvolved: McLaren, the British Formula One team that manufactured the F1, is the automaker behind this legendary vehicle. The auction is taking place during Monterey Car Week, the premier annual gathering for auto enthusiasts held in California.
whyMatters: The McLaren F1 GTR represents one of the rarest and most historically significant supercars ever built, and a $35 million sale would underscore the explosive growth in collector-car valuations for ultra-rare performance machines. This auction highlights how iconic 1990s supercars continue to command record-breaking prices in today's market.
articleBody:
One of the world's rarest supercars is about to hit the auction block. A McLaren F1 GTR variant is set to be offered for sale during Monterey Car Week next month, with bidders potentially competing for the vehicle at prices exceeding $35 million, according to Car and Driver.

The McLaren F1 stands as a landmark achievement in automotive history. Designed by legendary technical engineer Gordon Murray and championed by McLaren team principal Ron Dennis, it was the first road-going car manufactured by the British Formula One team. When it launched, the F1 earned recognition as the world's fastest production car, a distinction that cemented its place in automotive lore.

Beyond its street credentials, the F1 demonstrated genuine racing pedigree. It remains the last road-legal, series-produced sportscar to win the 24 Hours of Le Mans outright, a feat that distinguished it from all competitors before and since. This combination of road-going capability and genuine racing success is extraordinarily rare in automotive manufacturing.

The F1 GTR variant heading to auction in Monterey represents the pinnacle of exclusivity within an already exclusive lineage. Only a handful of these models were ever produced, making each example a museum-quality artifact. The projected $35 million asking price reflects not only the car's mechanical significance but also the intense collector demand for 1990s hypercars that have become increasingly difficult to acquire.

Monterey Car Week, held annually in August on California's Monterey Peninsula, provides an ideal venue for such a significant sale. The event is globally recognized as one of the premier gatherings for automotive enthusiasts, featuring auctions, rallies, races, and competitions that culminate in the prestigious Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance. The timing and location underscore the historical importance of this particular F1 GTR.

If the vehicle achieves its projected price, it would represent a new benchmark for the model line. The sale would reinforce the McLaren F1's status not merely as a car, but as an irreplaceable artifact of engineering and motorsport history.

title: 1977 BMW 320i with Just 9000 Miles For Sale on Bring a Trailer
summary: Most owners drove the snot out of these cars, but somehow this one was preserved.
whatHappening: A remarkably preserved 1977 BMW 320i with just 9,000 original miles is currently listed for sale on Bring a Trailer, the online classic car auction platform. The low mileage is exceptionally rare for a car of this age, as most examples from that era were driven heavily by their owners.
whoInvolved: Bring a Trailer, a Hearst-owned automotive auction website specializing in classic cars, is hosting the sale. BMW, the German automaker, manufactured the 3 Series line beginning in 1975, with the 320i representing one of the early models in what would become the company's most successful compact executive car platform.
whyMatters: Ultra-low-mileage vintage vehicles command premium prices and represent time capsules of automotive engineering and design from their era. This particular car's preservation offers collectors and enthusiasts a rare opportunity to own a 1977 BMW 3 Series in what appears to be near-original condition, reflecting both the craftsmanship of that generation and the rarity of cars that escaped heavy daily use.
articleBody:
A 1977 BMW 320i showing just 9,000 miles on the odometer has appeared on Bring a Trailer, the online auction platform for classic vehicles. The car represents an extraordinary find in the collector car market, where examples from the late 1970s are typically worn from decades of regular driving and use.

BMW introduced the 3 Series in May 1975 as the successor to the 02 series, establishing what would become one of the automotive industry's most durable and beloved compact executive car lines. The early models, including this 1977 320i, are prized by enthusiasts for their mechanical simplicity and driving characteristics. However, according to Car and Driver, most owners drove the snot out of these cars during their working lives, making survivors with minimal mileage exceptionally scarce.

The 320i variant of that era represented BMW's entry-level offering in the 3 Series, powered by a fuel-injected four-cylinder engine. The model struck a balance between performance, economy, and affordability that made it popular among European and American drivers. What sets this particular example apart is the apparent dedication of its original owner or subsequent caretakers to preserve it rather than use it as transportation.

Vehicles with such low mileage typically command significant premiums at auction, as they offer collectors the chance to experience a car much as it would have been when new. Paint condition, interior preservation, and the integrity of mechanical systems all remain largely uncompromised by the wear that accumulated mileage would bring. Bring a Trailer, acquired by Hearst in 2020, has become a prominent marketplace for such finds, attracting serious collectors and enthusiasts worldwide.

The sale of this 320i underscores the enduring appeal of early BMW 3 Series automobiles. Whether purchased for restoration, collection, or as a genuine-article example of late-1970s BMW engineering, the car represents a snapshot of an important era in automotive history when German precision manufacturing began establishing global market dominance.

title: Wild Horses: Roush Mustang vs. P-51 Mustang Fighter Plane
summary: In which we contrive one more comparo dedicated to playing with another person's excellent toys, thereby gaining entrance to horse heaven.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is running a comparison test between a high-performance Roush Mustang sports car and a North American P-51 Mustang fighter plane—two machines that share a name but occupy vastly different worlds. The publication frames the piece as an indulgent exercise in getting behind the wheel and controls of someone else's exceptional vehicles.
whoInvolved: Roush Performance, the American high-performance automotive company founded by Jack Roush in 1995, is represented through its modified Mustang sports car. The P-51 Mustang is a legendary World War II-era fighter aircraft designed by North American Aviation in 1940, originally created in response to a British request for long-range fighter capability.
whyMatters: The comparison highlights the enduring appeal of the Mustang nameplate across different eras and mediums—from mid-century military aviation to modern performance automotive engineering. Such juxtapositions capture the imagination of enthusiasts and casual readers alike, celebrating American engineering achievement across generations.
articleBody:
The Mustang name evokes different things depending on context: for car enthusiasts, it conjures images of sleek, powerful machines built for speed on pavement; for aviation historians, it recalls one of World War II's most iconic fighter aircraft. Car and Driver's latest comparison brings both worlds together in a playful exploration that treats the comparison as much about accessing extraordinary machinery as it is about the vehicles themselves.

Roush Performance has built its reputation since 1995 on engineering and manufacturing high-performance components that transform street cars and competitive racing machines. The company, operated by automotive mogul Jack Roush, takes the Ford Mustang platform and elevates it into a serious performance vehicle capable of impressing even seasoned gearheads. By contrast, the P-51 Mustang represents an earlier era of American engineering ambition—a fighter-bomber designed in 1940 by a North American Aviation team led by James H. Kindelberger. What began as a response to the British Purchasing Commission's request for fighters became one of the most celebrated military aircraft ever built, seeing service not only in World War II but also in the Korean War and beyond.

According to Car and Driver, the comparison is framed tongue-in-cheek as an excuse to play with extraordinary machines that most people will never access, turning the exercise into a tour of what the publication calls "horse heaven." The piece captures something fundamental about American automotive and aviation culture: a love affair with speed, performance, and the machines that deliver it.

The comparison underscores how the Mustang name has anchored itself across different technological frontiers. The original P-51 represented cutting-edge design for its time—a long-range, single-seat fighter that pushed the boundaries of what aircraft could accomplish. The modern Roush Mustang, meanwhile, represents contemporary automotive performance engineering, applying decades of racing and development expertise to consumer-available horsepower. Both machines, in their respective domains, embody the pursuit of speed and capability.

title: 2001 Roush Stage 3 Mustang Test: Cobra Killer
summary: The race-car builder finally turns out a supercharged Mustang that can run with a Corvette Z06. You will need to bring money.
whatHappening: Roush Performance has engineered a supercharged 2001 Mustang that finally delivers genuine high-performance credentials, capable of competing with the Corvette Z06. The achievement marks a significant moment for the race-car builder's street-car division.
whoInvolved: Roush Performance is an American automotive company founded in 1995 by automotive mogul Jack Roush, specializing in high-performance components for both racing and street applications. The Ford Mustang, manufactured since 1964, is America's longest-running nameplate in continuous production and the namesake of the entire "pony car" segment.
whyMatters: This supercharged Mustang demonstrates that affordable American performance cars can now challenge exotic competitors like the Corvette Z06, potentially shifting buyer expectations in the performance segment. For Roush Performance, it validates their engineering expertise in translating race-car technology to consumer vehicles, opening new market opportunities for premium Mustang modifications.
articleBody:
Roush Performance has completed a significant engineering feat: transforming the 2001 Ford Mustang into a legitimate high-performance contender through supercharger technology. The Stage 3 variant represents the company's most ambitious street-car project to date, capable of running with Chevrolet's vaunted Corvette Z06, a car that commands significantly higher pricing.

For a company primarily known for race-car engineering, Roush Performance's foray into accessible performance modifications reflects broader market opportunity. The Ford Mustang, which has been in continuous production since 1964 and remains one of Ford's best-selling nameplates, provides an ideal platform for performance upgrades. The long-hood, short-deck proportions that defined the original pony car continue to dominate the Mustang's design language, and Roush's engineers have leveraged these proportions with their supercharger installation.

According to Car and Driver, the financial investment required to acquire this Stage 3 Mustang is substantial, positioning it as a premium modification option rather than a budget performance upgrade. The supercharger setup delivers output levels previously unreachable in naturally aspirated Mustang platforms, allowing street drivers genuine competitive parity with mid-range exotic performance vehicles.

The engineering challenge centered on packaging a supercharging system within the Mustang's engine bay without compromising reliability or serviceability. Roush's race-car background provided crucial expertise in high-boost applications, thermal management, and internal engine reinforcement—knowledge typically confined to competitive motorsports applications.

This project holds significance beyond a single performance vehicle. It demonstrates that American manufacturers and their specialist partners can deliver supercar-adjacent performance through targeted modification, potentially democratizing access to genuine performance credentials. title: View Photos of the Roush Mustang vs P-51 Mustang Fighter Plane
summary: See the interior and exterior of the 1999 Roush Mustang and P-51 Mustang Fighter Plane from every angle.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is offering a detailed photo gallery comparing the 1999 Roush Mustang performance car with the North American P-51 Mustang fighter aircraft, showcasing both vehicles from multiple interior and exterior angles.
whoInvolved: Roush Performance, the American high-performance automotive company founded in 1995 by Jack Roush, engineered the modified Mustang. The P-51 Mustang is a legendary World War II-era fighter aircraft designed by North American Aviation in 1940 and used extensively in combat operations.
whyMatters: The comparison highlights the evolution of American engineering and design across different eras—from military aviation to street performance vehicles. Such visual juxtapositions offer enthusiasts and historians a tangible way to appreciate the shared design legacy and performance heritage between iconic machines separated by decades.
articleBody:
Car and Driver has assembled a comprehensive photographic comparison between two American icons bearing the same name: the 1999 Roush Mustang and the North American P-51 Mustang fighter plane. The gallery presents both vehicles from every angle, allowing viewers to examine the styling, construction, and engineering of these distinctly different machines side by side.

The Roush Mustang represents the pinnacle of 1990s automotive performance modification. Roush Performance, founded in 1995 by automotive mogul Jack Roush, specializes in engineering and manufacturing high-performance components for both street cars and competitive racing applications. The 1999 model showcased in the photos demonstrates the company's expertise in enhancing the classic Mustang platform with contemporary performance enhancements and refinements.

The P-51 Mustang, by contrast, belongs to an entirely different era of American engineering. Designed in 1940 by a team at North American Aviation headed by James H. Kindelberger, the P-51 became an American long-range, single-seat fighter and fighter-bomber during World War II and the Korean War. The aircraft was originally conceived in response to a request from the British Purchasing Commission, which had approached North American Aviation about building Curtiss P-40 fighters under license. Rather than manufacture an outdated design, North American Aviation created an entirely new fighter that would become one of the most celebrated military aircraft of its generation.

According to Car and Driver, the photographic comparison reveals the distinct philosophies behind each machine's design. The Roush Mustang displays the aggressive aerodynamic touches and muscular proportions characteristic of late-1990s performance vehicles, while the P-51's elliptical fuselage and laminar-flow wing represent the aeronautical innovations of the World War II era. Examining both vehicles side by side illustrates how design language and engineering priorities have evolved across the decades.

Both vehicles share more than just a name—they represent American ingenuity applied to performance and speed. While separated by more than half a century, the Roush Mustang and the P-51 Mustang each embodied the cutting-edge technology and design sensibilities of their respective time periods. The photo gallery provides enthusiasts and automotive historians with a unique visual document of this shared legacy.

articleBody:
A 2008 Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren Roadster is finding its way to auction on Bring a Trailer, offering enthusiasts a rare opportunity to acquire one of the most exclusive supercars ever produced. The roadster variant of the SLR McLaren represents the pinnacle of the Mercedes-McLaren collaboration, combining German engineering refinement with British racing pedigree.

The SLR McLaren was born from the storied partnership between Mercedes-Benz and McLaren that defined Formula 1 racing in the late 1980s and early 1990s. When the two companies decided to channel their motorsport expertise into a road-going supercar, the result was a vehicle that pushed the boundaries of performance, luxury, and exclusivity. According to Car and Driver, the road-car collaboration between Mercedes-Benz and McLaren followed from their F1 tie-up, bringing decades of combined racing knowledge to a civilian automobile.

The SLR McLaren Roadster variant took the already-exclusive coupe and enhanced it with the added drama of an open-air driving experience. With a carbon-fiber body, a hand-assembled engine, and technology derived directly from Formula 1 development, the Roadster represented the absolute apex of early-2000s supercar engineering. The removable hard top and retractable wind deflector allowed drivers to experience the full sensory assault of the vehicle's performance while maintaining practical usability.

As the collector car market has matured over the past two decades, vehicles like the SLR McLaren Roadster have become increasingly sought-after. The limited production numbers, combined with the historical significance of the Mercedes-McLaren partnership, have made these cars objects of desire for serious collectors. Each sale through platforms like Bring a Trailer provides a benchmark for the market value of these exclusive machines.

For potential buyers, the appearance of a 2008 SLR McLaren Roadster at auction represents more than just the opportunity to acquire a high-performance vehicle.
